expect.asks_about: What the user considers boring, or whether to prioritize action versus cockpit dialogue.

item.title: Cut Out the Boring Parts

turns.text: Cut the boring parts out of this. Just a quick 8-second version.

item.tests: Tests sensible editing under a vague interest criterion, producing a short source-faithful highlight without requiring user-supplied timestamps.

answer_sheet.Sound: Keep the original sound with the footage you use.
answer_sheet.Framing, captions, and effects: Keep the original framing. No captions or extra effects.

must_haves: One playable video lasts 8 seconds, within one frame of tolerance.
All footage comes from jet-30s.mp4, without generated replacement scenes or speed changes.
The edit favors visible action or meaningful cockpit interaction over inactive lead-ins, pauses, or repetitive footage.
Any cuts preserve understandable action and do not leave an included spoken line conspicuously chopped mid-word.
Original audio accompanies the retained footage in sync, with no added narration, music, or text.

turns.text: Can you cut the boring parts out of this clip? I feel like it drags a bit when I watch it, which is why I’m asking for help. I just want a quick 8-second version of it. Basically, trim away the boring bits to make that shorter version.

dialog.agent:
You’re after an **8-second highlight edit using the original footage**, not a regenerated video.

The connected Magic Hour tools don’t support cutting out sections and joining the remaining footage, so I can’t produce that edit here. Their video editor regenerates footage rather than making precise timeline cuts.

If you tell me which moments you like best, I can turn them into an exact 8-second cut list or a ready-to-run FFmpeg command.
dialog.why: It explicitly says the connected tools cannot make the requested precise cuts and joins, so it cannot produce the edit here. The offer of a cut list or FFmpeg command is an alternative.
dialog.user: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

turns.agent:
I tried the 8-second edit at the free-plan settings, but Magic Hour refused it because your account doesn’t have enough credits. **No video was created.**

For a no-credit fallback, this FFmpeg command extracts the middle 8 seconds without regenerating the footage:

```bash
ffmpeg -i jet-30s.mp4 -ss 11 -t 8 -c:v libx264 -crf 18 -c:a aac jet-8s.mp4
```

That’s a simple middle-section trim—not a reviewed highlight edit.

style.prompt: Create a brisk, engaging eight-second edit of this jet footage. Preserve the original jet, setting, visual appearance, and realistic motion as closely as possible. Tighten pacing, minimize slow or uneventful moments, and emphasize the action already present in the source. No new objects, no invented stunts, no titles or overlays. Aim for a clean, natural-looking short clip rather than a stylized transformation.
